## The stock-market challenge

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import datetime as dt
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

BLUE = "#2563eb"
GREEN = "#16a34a"
PURPLE = "#9333ea"
ORANGE = "#ea580c"
RED = "#dc2626"
YELLOW = "#eab308"
INK = "#172033"
MUTED = "#64748b"
GRID = "#dbe3ec"

plt.rcParams.update(
    {
        "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
        "font.size": 14,
        "axes.titlesize": 18,
        "axes.labelsize": 13,
        "axes.edgecolor": "#cbd5e1",
        "axes.labelcolor": MUTED,
        "xtick.color": MUTED,
        "ytick.color": MUTED,
        "grid.color": GRID,
        "grid.linewidth": 0.8,
        "figure.facecolor": "white",
        "axes.facecolor": "white",
    }
)

rows = []
with Path("data/sp500_fred.csv").open() as source:
    for row in csv.DictReader(source):
        if row["SP500"] not in ("", "."):
            rows.append(
                (
                    dt.date.fromisoformat(row["observation_date"]),
                    float(row["SP500"]),
                )
            )

dates = np.array([row[0] for row in rows], dtype=object)
prices = np.array([row[1] for row in rows], dtype=float)

def rmse(observed, predicted):
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean((observed - predicted) ** 2)))

def r_squared(observed, predicted):
    residual = np.sum((observed - predicted) ** 2)
    total = np.sum((observed - observed.mean()) ** 2)
    return float(1 - residual / total)
```

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}

::: {.prompt-panel}
**Prompt to an AI assistant**

> Download historical S&P 500 prices. Use recent prices to predict the next day's closing price. Show me how the predictions compare with what actually happened.
:::

An AI assistant can generate the code in seconds.

::: {.question-callout}
Would you use the result to invest your own money?
:::

:::
::: {.column width="58%"}

```{python}
#| label: market-history
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.9
#| out-width: 100%

history = (dates >= dt.date(2017, 1, 1)) & (dates <= dt.date(2024, 12, 31))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.9))
ax.plot(dates[history], prices[history], color=BLUE, linewidth=2.6)
ax.fill_between(dates[history], prices[history], prices[history].min(), color=BLUE, alpha=0.08)
ax.set_title("S&P 500 daily closing level")
ax.set_ylabel("Index level")
ax.grid(axis="y")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator(2))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y"))
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

:::
:::

::: {.source-note}
Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC via FRED, series SP500. The teaching example is not investment advice.
:::

::: {.notes}
开场先让学生判断，不解释答案。重点不是股票知识，而是让学生体验“代码已经可以自动生成，但判断仍然没有自动完成”。
:::

## AI can build the prediction in seconds

```{python}
#| label: fit-model
#| include: false

lag_count = 5
X = np.array([
    prices[i-lag_count:i][::-1]
    for i in range(lag_count, len(prices))
])
y = prices[lag_count:]
model_dates = dates[lag_count:]

train = model_dates < dt.date(2020, 1, 1)
test = ((model_dates >= dt.date(2020, 1, 1)) &
        (model_dates <= dt.date(2024, 12, 31)))

X_train = np.c_[np.ones(train.sum()), X[train]]
X_test = X[test]
beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X_train, y[train], rcond=None)[0]
prediction = np.c_[np.ones(test.sum()), X_test] @ beta
actual = y[test]
test_dates = model_dates[test]
naive_prediction = X_test[:, 0]
actual_change = actual - naive_prediction
predicted_change = prediction - naive_prediction
```

::: {.plain-steps}
<div class="blue-step"><span>01</span><b>Give AI the task</b><p>Use earlier prices to predict the next day's closing price.</p></div>
<div class="green-step"><span>02</span><b>AI writes the program</b><p>It prepares the data, builds a prediction rule, and produces a result for each day.</p></div>
<div class="purple-step"><span>03</span><b>Hide the future</b><p>The program predicts one day at a time without seeing that day's answer.</p></div>
<div class="orange-step"><span>04</span><b>Compare with reality</b><p>We repeat the check across five years of market data.</p></div>
:::

::: {.question-callout}
If the predicted line follows the real market, has AI solved the problem?
:::

::: {.notes}
不展示代码细节。只用普通语言说明：AI 写出了程序，我们让它在看不到答案的情况下预测，然后与真实结果比较。
:::

## The prediction looks remarkable

```{python}
#| label: prediction-overlay
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| out-width: 100%

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12.5, 5.6))
ax.plot(test_dates, actual, color=INK, linewidth=3.0, label="What actually happened")
ax.plot(test_dates, prediction, color=GREEN, linewidth=2.0, alpha=0.9, label="AI-generated prediction")
ax.set_ylabel("S&P 500 closing level")
ax.grid(axis="y")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator())
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y"))
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", ncol=2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.green-takeaway}
Across five years, the two lines are almost impossible to separate.
:::

::: {.notes}
让学生先看整段五年结果。不要解释误差指标，再次询问他们现在是否愿意相信模型。
:::

## Yesterday's price looks just as good

::: {.baseline-rule}
The simple rule: use today's closing price as tomorrow's prediction.
:::

```{python}
#| label: baseline-overlay
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 5.25
#| out-width: 100%

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12.5, 5.25))
ax.plot(test_dates, actual, color=INK, linewidth=3.0, label="What actually happened")
ax.plot(test_dates, naive_prediction, color=BLUE, linewidth=2.0, alpha=0.9, label="Yesterday's closing price")
ax.set_ylabel("S&P 500 closing level")
ax.grid(axis="y")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator())
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y"))
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", ncol=2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.red-takeaway}
The picture alone does not show that the AI model knows more than yesterday's price.
:::

::: {.notes}
这里完成认知反转。简单规则没有训练模型，却产生了几乎一样漂亮的图。重点不是宣布 AI 模型完全无效，而是说明“看起来贴合”还不足以支持原来的结论。
:::

## The difficult part is the change

```{python}
#| label: movement-comparison
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 5.3
#| out-width: 100%

focus = test_dates >= dt.date(2024, 10, 1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12.5, 5.3))
ax.plot(test_dates[focus], actual_change[focus], color=INK, linewidth=2.5, label="What the market changed by")
ax.plot(test_dates[focus], predicted_change[focus], color=ORANGE, linewidth=2.1, label="What the model expected")
ax.axhline(0, color="#94a3b8", linewidth=1.2)
ax.set_ylabel("Change from the previous day")
ax.grid(axis="y")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator())
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b"))
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", ncol=2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.contrast-line}
<div><b>The easy part</b><span>Today's level is usually close to yesterday's.</span></div>
<div><b>The useful part</b><span>Can we anticipate what changes next?</span></div>
:::

::: {.notes}
先用普通语言解释“变化”：今天相对昨天上升或下降了多少。投资决策更关心新增变化，而这张图显示模型没有稳定跟上真实变化。第一课不引入 return、direction accuracy 或其他技术指标。
:::

## Five questions for every data problem {.philosophy-slide}

::: {.five-questions}
<div class="blue-question"><span>01</span><b>What are we trying to predict or decide?</b><small>Start from the real problem. Is machine learning the right tool?</small></div>
<div class="green-question"><span>02</span><b>What data can we use?</b><small>Is it available at that moment, relevant, and trustworthy?</small></div>
<div class="orange-question"><span>03</span><b>What would count as a good answer?</b><small>Choose a standard that matches the decision.</small></div>
<div class="purple-question"><span>04</span><b>How will we find a better rule?</b><small>Use data to improve the model.</small></div>
<div class="yellow-question"><span>05</span><b>What evidence would make us trust it?</b><small>Compare it with reality and a sensible alternative.</small></div>
:::

::: {.course-purpose}
<b>Machine learning learns a rule from examples and uses it on new cases.</b>
<span>This course teaches you how to judge whether that rule solves the real problem.</span>
:::

::: {.notes}
这是课程设计哲学的第一页。先明确：不是所有问题都需要机器学习，数据是否相关、当时是否可得、是否可信，也属于建模的一部分。页面底部用一句直觉定义帮助初学者理解机器学习；这是对许多监督学习问题的第一层理解，后续无监督学习等内容会逐步扩展它。暂时不用 formalisation、loss、optimisation 等术语。
:::

## The problems become harder and more realistic

::: {.course-map}
<div class="blue-map"><span>01</span><div><b>Predict a number</b><small>A first complete problem</small></div><p>How many rentals, how much demand, or what value comes next?</p></div>
<div class="green-map"><span>02</span><div><b>Support a decision</b><small>Choose between possible outcomes</small></div><p>Will something happen, and how certain are we?</p></div>
<div class="purple-map"><span>03</span><div><b>Find structure without answers</b><small>No answer is provided</small></div><p>Which patterns or groups are present in the data?</p></div>
<div class="orange-map"><span>04</span><div><b>Discover useful features</b><small>Images and other complex data</small></div><p>Can the model learn what information matters?</p></div>
:::

::: {.course-contract}
<div class="shared-path"><b>One sequence, five questions</b><span>Each stage begins where the previous method stops being enough.</span></div>
<div class="mps311"><b>MPS311</b><span>Understand, apply, and explain.</span></div>
<div class="mps439"><b>MPS439</b><span>Derive, implement, and test the limits.</span></div>
:::

::: {.notes}
这是课程设计哲学的第二页。强调课程不是无端更换算法，而是问题逐步变难、更接近现实；每个新方法都回应上一种方法的限制。两门课共享同一条问题主线，但要求的深度不同：MPS311 重在理解、应用与解释，MPS439 还要继续推导、实现并检验假设和边界。两门课都通过实际问题学习，行政安排留在课程网站。
:::

## Machine learning after large language models

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.blue-panel .tall-panel}
<p class="panel-title">An AI assistant can help you</p>

- write and debug code
- try a model quickly
- make graphs and tables
- explain unfamiliar syntax
:::

:::
::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.purple-panel .tall-panel}
<p class="panel-title">You remain responsible for</p>

- the question worth answering
- the information available
- what a good answer means
- which comparison is fair
- what the evidence supports
:::

:::
:::

::: {.green-takeaway}
AI makes implementation faster. You still decide whether the result answers the right question.
:::

::: {.llm-question}
<b>The same questions apply to an AI system</b>
<span>What did it learn from? What was it asked to produce? What evidence supports using it here?</span>
:::

::: {.notes}
正面承认 AI 的能力。避免使用 objective、optimisation 等尚未解释的术语。本页回答学生为什么仍然需要学习机器学习，并说明相同的五个问题也可以用来检查 AI 系统本身。
:::

## Before you trust a model {.final-slide}

::: {.exit-question}
A model draws a stock-price line that almost perfectly matches the real line.

**What is the first question you would ask?**
:::

::: {.class-rhythm}
<div><b>Lecture</b><span>Build the reasoning</span></div>
<div><b>Lab</b><span>Reconstruct it with data and code</span></div>
<div><b>AI</b><span>Use it, test it, inspect it, explain it</span></div>
:::

::: {.closing-line}
A good model begins with a well-formed question.
:::

::: {.notes}
让学生提交一句话答案。可以接受真实问题、预测对象、简单比较、时间信息或证据等不同切入点，然后说明本学期会反复训练这种判断。
:::
